subject: ventures/photo-editing
auditor: agent session (Claude), third round; no fix landed since the 2026-11-08 audit
professional: a working event/wedding photographer who also edits video (culls 2,000 frames after a shoot, grades with LUTs, cuts reels); first checks: is luma/exposure read on a standard, is the sharp-at-100% pick right and are deliberate low-key frames spared, is the tilt reading right, is the public page truthful about what runs

evidence.correctness: Ran the code and recomputed with numpy 2.4.6 (platform/ci/pyenv.py), not the author's tests. (a) Three frames at 320x180 (uniform random, gradient+Gaussian noise sigma 7, 20 px blocks): shootflow.frame_analysis._laplacian_variance 109413.72085046367 / 994.405076567896 / 2212.9032577203025 vs numpy 4-neighbour Laplacian .var() identical to every printed digit; noise_sigma_from_frame 76.3528539 / 7.1658018 / 0.0 vs numpy median(|Immerkaer response|)/(0.6745*6) identical. (b) dhash_hex vs independent numpy 9x8 box-average, bit=left>right: e9155599bc25759a = e9155599bc25759a, 0000000000000000 = 0000000000000000, 28f6f24cdcb39530 = 28f6f24cdcb39530. (c) mean_luma, exposure and contrast from metrics_from_frames vs the documented formulas in numpy: 127.239/0.822084/1.0, 124.518/0.962351/0.866732, 129.215/0.820628/1.0, all equal. (d) Colour to luma through the real ffmpeg path (analyze_media on solid-colour PNGs made with ffmpeg lavfi): red 76, green 149, blue 29, grey 128, orange 151 vs ITU-R BT.601 full-range Y=.299R+.587G+.114B: 76.24, 149.69, 29.07, 128.0, 151.38 (agree within 1 level); vs BT.709 (what sRGB/Rec.709 content uses): red 54.2, green 182.4, blue 18.4, so the tool silently measures exposure in BT.601, which departs from 709 by up to 28 levels on saturated colours. (e) Tilt: analytic sigmoid edges at true 0, 1.5, -4, 8, -12 deg read 0.0, 1.491, -3.991, 7.987, -11.975 deg (confidence 0.997-1.0); a vertical edge at 3 deg read 2.994; pure noise read 0.70 deg at confidence 0.036 (low confidence flags it). Numbers are right on synthetic media; no real RAW/camera file, so capped at 3.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: cull (ran last two rounds, code unchanged), tilt/noise/dHash/luma/framing metrics (ran, correct), colour->luma via ffmpeg decode (ran, works), RAW preview scoring (synthetic only, per README). Not re-run this round: execute-ingest, run-local-pipeline, launchd plist, reels/carousels (README claims them as working; they were exercised in the 2026-11-07 round and the pipeline code is unchanged). Stated gaps stand (no RAW development, no app). `git log -- ventures/photo-editing/site` shows the last site change is ca9a4d0b, an unrelated shift-roster commit; no fix to the audited defects. 3 against its own README; the page, not the README, is the incomplete party.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/photo-editing && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 517 tests, 21-30 s, FAILED (failures=1, errors=1, skipped=1), identical to the previous round. The failure is test_workspace_health.test_unreadable_render_input_is_reported_for_review (chmod(0) is a no-op as root, line 117); the error is test_real_photo_calibration.test_tilt_crop_removes_corners_and_keeps_aspect (system Pillow's _imaging missing, no importorskip). Five seeded mutations, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards): M1 frame_analysis.py exposure target 120 -> 100: suite result identical to baseline, NOT caught. M2 _SHARPNESS_HALF_POINT 60 -> 600 (sharpness score collapses tenfold): identical to baseline, NOT caught. M3 dhash comparison > flipped to <: NOT caught (note the flip complements every hash, so burst grouping by Hamming distance is unchanged; near-equivalent mutation, but no test pins the bit order either). M4 cull.BLURRY_BELOW 0.2 -> 0.0: CAUGHT (failures 1 -> 9). M5 cull.NEAR_DUPLICATE_MAX_DISTANCE 8 -> 30: CAUGHT (failures 1 -> 7). So the cull's decision thresholds are pinned but the measurement layer that feeds them (exposure centre, sharpness scale) is not, the same M1 gap as the previous two rounds, still open. 2.
evidence.craft: Read frame_analysis.py (metrics_from_frames, framing, noise, dhash, Laplacian, luma stats) and cull.py (grouping, role assignment). Readable, documented formulas, named constants, typed dataclasses. Defects: pure-Python per-pixel loops (Laplacian, noise, framing, each a full 57k-pixel pass in Python; noise sorts the whole response list for a median) with no numpy path; magic weights (0.6/0.4 framing, 0.85/0.15 technical, 120.0 grey target hard-coded inline) uncalibrated; luma colour matrix is whatever ffmpeg's gray conversion uses and is not documented in the code; 23,408 lines in src/shootflow with a parallel dry-run adapter/scheduler stack beside the real ffmpeg path; `ruff check src tests`: 69 errors (41 auto-fixable), unchanged. Two tests fail in a root or minimal sandbox without guards.
evidence.claims: Public page ventures/photo-editing/site/index.html is unchanged since the last two audits. Line 40 'The renderers are dry-run placeholders: ShootFlow does not yet render video or grade images' and line 51 'No. The renderers are dry-run placeholders' contradict the README ('turn an ingested shoot into real media ... graded/ ... instagram_reel.mp4') and llms.txt ('makes review proxies, applies the user's 3D LUT ... cuts 1080x1920 Instagram reels'), both of which describe code that exists and was run in round 1. Lines 34 and 47 tell users to run `shootflow cull FOLDER --out REPORT`; pyproject.toml declares no console script (grep scripts pyproject.toml: none), so the copy-paste command fails and the working form is `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m shootflow.cli cull`. llms.txt repeats the non-installed `shootflow cull` form and links the old duckduckgo/github.io address rather than https://marisstella.app/photo-editing/. Backed claims: cull behaviour, XMP star mapping (keeper 4, alternate 2, reject -1, cull.py _SIDECAR_RATING), no upload, 'not yet measured on a real wedding shoot' honesty. Three public surfaces disagree with each other on whether it renders. 2.
evidence.fitness: Job: cull a shoot folder and get a ranked, XMP-tagged selection, then optionally grade and cut reels. The cull and metrics run offline and correctly on synthetic data, and the calibration docs in eval/ show tilt measured on real photos. But the user has to find the PYTHONPATH invocation because the page gives a command that does not exist, there is no UI, RAW is scored from the embedded preview only and cannot go through grade, exposure is judged on BT.601 mean luma against a fixed grey, and nothing has been validated against a human's picks on a real shoot (VENTURE.yaml stage prototype). A photographer could try it as a first pass. 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against Photo Mechanic/Lightroom cull practice (judge focus at 100%, one keeper per burst, spare deliberate low-key frames) and ITU-R BT.709/BT.601 luma practice. Sound: sha256-verified non-destructive ingest, XMP rating semantics, dHash burst grouping, Immerkaer noise estimation, structure-tensor tilt, all matching their published definitions in my recomputation. Departures: analysis on a 320x180 gray downscale cannot see critical-focus misses; exposure is mean luma versus a fixed 120 with a clipping penalty so deliberate low-key or high-key frames score as bad; luma is BT.601 whereas sRGB/Rec.709 stills and video use 709 (red 76 versus 54), so exposure of saturated colour is mis-weighted; no colour-managed (ICC or log) reading. A pro would use it as a first pass, not sign off the cull.

defects.what: Public page says the renderers are dry-run placeholders and that ShootFlow does not render video or grade images, contradicting the README and llms.txt; it also tells users to run a `shootflow` command that is not installed (no console script in pyproject.toml). Unchanged across three audit rounds.

Exposure grey target (120 to 100) and sharpness half-point (60 to 600) can be mutated with no test failing; only the cull thresholds downstream are pinned. Same exposure gap reported in rounds 1 and 2.

Exposure and contrast are computed from ffmpeg's gray conversion, which is BT.601 full range, not BT.709; saturated colours are mis-weighted (red 76 vs 54, green 149 vs 182) and the code never says which matrix it assumes. Plus mean-luma exposure and a 320x180 downscale penalise low-key frames and hide focus misses.
llms.txt still links the old github.io page instead of https://marisstella.app/photo-editing/ and repeats the non-installed `shootflow cull` form.
Two tests fail in a root/minimal sandbox without a guard: chmod(0) test as root, and a Pillow-dependent calibration test with no importorskip.
ruff reports 69 errors; per-pixel pure-Python loops with a full sort for the noise median; duplicated dry-run engine.

verdict: A third look, with no fix landed since round 2. The numeric core again reproduces against independent numpy code (Laplacian, Immerkaer noise, dHash, luma, exposure, contrast to every printed digit; tilt within 0.03 degrees across -12 to 8 degrees), and colour luma through ffmpeg matches BT.601 within one level, though that is not the BT.709 matrix a modern photographer's files use. It still does not meet the bar. The public page says it does not render or grade (false against README and llms.txt) and gives a command that is not installed, so claims stays 2, and three of five seeded mutations pass the suite, including the exposure target flagged twice before, so verification stays 2. Correctness and completeness are 3 on synthetic media; the rest are 2 because nothing has been tried on a real shoot and the highest-severity defect, a one-file page edit, has now survived three rounds.
